land.text: Qingtang, renamed Xining, annexed from Tsongkha in 1103

successors.note: 'In 1103 the Song dispatched Wang Hou to conquer Tsongkha ... the Song armies occupied the region again and renamed Qingtang to Xining' (Tsongkha page); the infobox says disestablished 1104. Hezhou had gone to the Song in 1072. The Western Xia took the Qingtang area in 1113 on the Song-Xia wars page and the Jin ceded it to the Xia in 1136 on the Tsongkha page (see the western-xia dossier).

capitals.name: Hezhou (Linxia)
capitals.note: 'The elders of Amdo found a Yarlung descendant in Gaochang and took him to Hezhou' in 997. Centre of the gazetteer's Linxia disc; the page does not say Hezhou is Linxia (researcher's identification, confidence 1). Kuozhou (1008) and Miaochuan (1025) are not in the gazetteer and are left out.

capitals.name: Qingtang (Xining)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Tsongkha (Ping'an District), Qingtang (Xining); 'in 1032 relocated to Qingtang'. Centre of the gazetteer's Xining disc.

rulers.name: Gusiluo (Gyelse)
rulers.note: Found in Gaochang and taken to Hezhou in 997; 'enthroned at Kuozhou as Tsenpo' in 1008; died 1065 (the Gusiluo page gives '997-1065' as his years).

rulers.name: Dongzhan
rulers.note: Succeeded in 1065; died 1086. Killed his brothers Xiazhan and Mozhanjiao after a Khitan princess was married to him in 1058.

rulers.name: Aligu
rulers.note: The page names him after Dongzhan's death in 1086 and gives the next ruler in 1096.

rulers.name: Longza
rulers.note: Enthroned in 1099; Song commander Wang Shan defeated him; the Song 'conquered' Tsongkha in 1103. The page has him renamed Zhao Huaide and raised to prince in 1108.

correction.text: a 100 km disc round Hezhou (Linxia), the seat of the Gusiluo's lordship until 1031

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its Tibetans row stops at 101.77 E, east of which Xining and Linxia lie outside every Cliopatria shape). 997: 'the elders of Amdo found a Yarlung descendant in Gaochang and took him to Hezhou'; 1008 he is enthroned at Kuozhou as Tsenpo; 1025 he moves to Miaochuan. The page gives no area and no boundary, so a disc round Hezhou (Linxia) stands in (confidence 1).

Hezhou is dropped; the Qingtang (Xining) disc remains until 1103. The Gusiluo page names Zongge (Ping'an District) as the confederacy's centre, inside this disc.

region.text: Hezhou (Linxia), where the elders took the Yarlung descendant

ledger.note: 997: 'The elders of Amdo found a Yarlung descendant in Gaochang and took him to Hezhou' (the infobox gives Established 997). He was named Gusiluo (Gyelse) and enthroned at Kuozhou as Tsenpo in 1008. The page is silent on the land held in 997, so the disc is a placeholder (confidence 1).
1032: the court 'relocated to Qingtang' (Xining) after a move to Miaochuan in 1025; his sons 'took Hezhou and Tsongkha'. The page does not say from whom.

ledger.note: 1065: Gusiluo dies and Dongzhan succeeds; 'Mucheng declared independence in Hezhou and sided with the Tanguts'.

notes:
State Cliopatria lacks: the Tibetans row (842-1249) ends at 101.77 E and no Cliopatria shape covers Xining or Linxia in 997-1103. Pages: Tsongkha and Gusiluo, plus the Song-Xia wars page (for 1113) read for the western-xia dossier; the Wang Shao page did not load.

The pages give no area and no boundary; regions are 100 km discs round the places they name. Identification of Hezhou with Linxia is the researcher's (the page does not say it). Kuozhou (1008) and Miaochuan (1025) are not in the gazetteer. Mucheng (1065-1072) was an independent lord in Hezhou, sided with the Tanguts and is only a counterpart name.

Disagreements: the infobox ends the kingdom in 1104 and the Song conquest is 1103; the Tsongkha page has the Song prince Zhao Huaide in 1108 and the Jin ceding the area to the Xia in 1136, while the Song-Xia wars page has the Xia taking the Qingtang region in 1113; the Gusiluo page gives the lifespan 997-1065, the Tsongkha page has his rule from 997 and his enthronement in 1008.
